title: Provisioning runway estimator and conditional approval matrix for dedicated reservations
creator: Ava Chen
description: Build a deterministic provisioning runway estimator and a conditional approval matrix to accelerate dedicated reservation requests. The estimator simulates capacity consumption, autoscale headroom, and cost/runway given a requested committed throughput (RPS/tokens/s) and expected traffic profile. The approval matrix encodes decision rules (auto-approve, requires-ops-review, requires-finance) driven by runway, SLO risk, multi-tenant contention, and contractual throughput guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: Estimator populates a per-request runway score (0-100) and a recommended approval lane (auto, ops-review, finance-review)
Estimator simulation accepts inputs: requested throughput, expected 95th latency target, burst multiplier, PKV cache hit rate, and quantization profile
Approval matrix rules are configurable via admin UI and expressed as readable conditions
Produce a lightweight CSV export of the simulation for sales/solutions reviews
Integrate estimator output into the provisioning intake UI and reservation email workflow
Add telemetry: per-simulation scores, inputs, decision reason codes, and post-provisioning utilization vs forecast
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Build a standalone estimator microservice (python) with a simple rule engine and a Docker image for local simulations
Phase 2: Integrate with intake form (Console) to show runway and flag recommended approval lane before submission
Phase 3: Hook into reservation state machine to attach decision rationale and links to simulation artifacts
Autoscale model: expose nominal headroom percent and dynamic burst policy; defaults are conservative (20% headroom, 2x burst) and tunable per-customer
Throughput guarantees modeled as committed tokens/s backed by dedicated pool sizing; estimator converts tokens to GPU-hours and cost delta vs shared-hosted baseline
Estimator should support scenario toggles: optimistic (high cache, aggressive batching) and conservative (low cache, minimal batching)
decision_log: 2025-02-20: Kickoff — consensus to prioritize runway estimator over UI polish to unblock sales
2025-02-24: Decided to represent runway as a single normalized score and a human-readable rationale string
2025-02-27: Ops requested a hard cap rule: auto-approve only when runway score > 70 and single-customer utilization projection < 60%
2025-03-01: Finance asked estimator to provide 12-month cost delta projection for committed vs pay-as-you-go
2025-03-02: Security reviewed data needs; decided to pseudonymize customer names in simulation logs stored in S3
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Estimator overfits to historical traces and underestimates burst risk — Mitigation: include stress tests with synthetic spikes and a conservative scenario
Risk: Sales may rely on auto-approve without reading constraints — Mitigation: make decision rationale prominent and require explicit acknowledgement for >P1 commitments
Risk: Model mismatch between estimator and runtime autoscaler — Mitigation: run a 2-week validation comparing forecast vs actual post-provisioning and tune parameters
Risk: Cost projections are misunderstood — Mitigation: surface assumptions and provide toggles (e.g., GPU pricing band) in the export
